status: Benefits now has a bounded native enrollment-workspace read: Company-scoped plans and enrollment windows, the current worker's dependents, reviewer-or-self enrollments with the retained People legal-name projection, package history enforcement and the retained write/review/document flags. The owner also has an owner-local HTTP router, a strict Next transport with personal-view forwarding, SSR/GET cutover and fail-closed native configuration. The Benefits owner remains pending overall: workspace membership, shared composition mounting, enrollment detail history/payroll, every plan/window/dependent/election command, attachments, learning eligibility, provider acknowledgement, payroll release, finance effects, jobs and browser acceptance remain open.

scope.workflowBoundary: The qualified slice is the Benefits workspace read used by the plans/enrollments/mine list views and the GET API: Company plans, enrollment windows, the active worker's dependents, reviewer-or-self enrollment rows, package history controls and the current write/review/document flags. Enrollment detail (history, payroll input, owner/provider document visibility), all plan/window/dependent/election commands, provider acknowledgement, payroll release, learning eligibility, attachments, finance effects and browser journeys remain retained TypeScript.
scope.domain: Current actor policy (records.read, explicit benefits module, work-context expiry, opaque 64-hex presentation context), exact Company scope, exact plan row shape (provider, coverage, currency, minor-unit money, effective range, status, version, reviewer, eligibility requirement), exact window row shape (ordered ISO dates, status, version, reviewer), exact dependent row shape (worker ownership, relationship, birth date, status, version), exact enrollment row shape (plan/window versions, coverage, money, effective range, status, version, plan name and People legal name), unique ids, deterministic updated_at-descending/id-ascending order, and explicit 500-plan / 500-window / 200-dependent / 1,000-election bounds that fail closed instead of truncating.
scope.application: One benefits_workspace use case checks the current actor before any package, worker or owner read; requires the current people.benefits history entitlement through a public Commercial port before source access; resolves the current active worker/engagement through a public People Payroll port; skips dependent reads when no worker exists; uses reviewer scope only for non-personal reads with benefits.review; always uses the current worker for the personal 'mine' view; requests the legal names of every distinct enrolled person once and requires a complete unique name projection; validates every row against the actor Company, worker and reviewer scope before presentation. Repository SQL stays on the caller's retained serializable Holding transaction.
scope.adapters: Read-only SQL over Benefits-owned benefit_plans, benefit_enrollment_windows, benefit_dependents and benefit_elections plus the Benefits-owned plan-name join. People worker and legal-name facts arrive only through the public BenefitsPeoplePort; no hr_people or hr_engagements SQL is authored here. Every read requires an existing transaction whose isolation is serializable; no transaction is opened, committed or retried. The adapter never creates, publishes, retires, verifies, submits, acknowledges, releases or deletes a Benefits or cross-owner row.
scope.http: Owner-local GET /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/benefits. Exact registered Host/Holding target keys and exact HTTPS origins, duplicate Host rejection, no query string, no request body, a strict optional x-erpx-benefits-personal: 1 scope flag with duplicate/unknown-value rejection, private/no-store plus no-referrer/nosniff responses, and bounded BusinessError status mapping. The composition backend receives transport facts only and must supply the normal Account session, live IAM authority, current Company/branch/department scope, package admission and serializable owner unit.
scope.transport: ERPX_NATIVE_BENEFITS_CONFIG is strictly validated: loopback-only private base, explicit port excluding 3000/3001/3100/3101/3103/5432/5433/5435/8080 and 3200-3299, exact HTTPS Holding origins, unique hosts/slugs, 250..30000 ms timeout, bounded cookie/context/workspace headers, exact plan/window/dependent/enrollment/purchase/context shapes, Company and worker-scope coherence, unique ordered rows, deterministic ordering, a 2 MiB response bound and no fallback on any configured failure.
scope.ssr: The workplace Benefits list page and the feature-people /benefits GET route use the native workspace when ERPX_NATIVE_BENEFITS_CONFIG is present. An unset configuration retains benefitsWorkspace; once configured, a malformed or failed native read is surfaced through the existing page/route error policy rather than silently replaced. The enrollment detail page, its benefitDetail history/payroll read, all POST commands and the BenefitsConsole document/command panels remain retained.
scope.purchaseAndIdentity: The native application requires the current people.benefits history entitlement through a public Commercial port when enforcement is enabled and projects the newWork/settleExisting/history/revision controls consumed by the retained console. This is a read projection, not an atomic owner unit; composition must repeat live IAM authority, the assignment module predicate, selected scope and purchase admission inside its own serializable owner transaction.
scope.writeBoundary: This slice is read-only. Versions are projected and validated, but there is no CAS mutation, idempotency receipt, audit event, outbox event, attachment binding, learning consumption, People Payroll handoff or Finance deferred effect in the native path. The retained TypeScript commands keep their current receipts, versions/CAS, idempotency, same-transaction People/Payroll/Finance guards, audit/outbox and rollback behavior.
scope.notClaimed: No browser journey, authenticated page render, shared composition mount, root workspace membership, catalogue acceptance qualification, enrollment detail/history/payroll read, command, provider acknowledgement, payroll release, attachment, learning eligibility, finance effect, job, staging, private production or Cloudflare verification.
